attacksRun.attack: The obligation set omits a leftover - the RESERVED or scoped surfaces are unaccounted for
attacksRun.evidence: Live v5 carries eight surfaces but the join names five obligations, so I checked whether S-ROLE (RESERVED), S-RUST2 (ADMITTED-UNSHIPPED) or S-STATE (ADMITTED-SCOPED) are leftovers the join drops. They are not the same kind of thing as the numeric windows. Each has a decided disposition inside v5: S-ROLE's skeleton reads 'Cannot invent roles beyond D-002 TypeScript. Additional roles enter by later slice', S-RUST2's reads 'Slice 1 does not ship this role (D-002)', and S-STATE is scoped to preview classes by the live DR-124 row. Their closures are specified content of the contract, which OBL-CONTRACT-V5 accounts for as 'The closed surface list ... are specified'. numericWindows is different in kind because v5 explicitly declines to mint the value and assigns it to a later product act with no owner today. Independently, the join's five obligations map one-to-one onto the dispositions D-103 actually recorded - OPEN, no SATISFIED, windows RESERVED, S-EVIDENCE deferred with DR-113, no lock producible - plus the extra-rows item, so nothing recorded is missing.

OBL-S-EVIDENCE carries rideStanding deferred-to-DR-113 and is bucketed under deferredOrRidesElsewhere, and doesNot carries 'Does not pull evidence/replay formats into slice 1.' This matches live v5, where the S-EVIDENCE surface has thisClosure DEFERRED and slice1 'no', with a skeleton warning that an unscoped reading 'would drag a DR-113-blocked surface into slice 1'. D-103 records the same: 'S-EVIDENCE remains deferred with DR-113.' The join marks it leftoverDesign false because it is deferred to another row, not because it is finished, which the rideStanding value makes explicit.

OBL-EXTRA-ROWS carries rideStanding specified-not-leftover and states that v5 names S-DOCTOR and S-SARIF as PROPOSED, not admitted. Live v5's proposedExtraRowsNotSelfAdmitted lists exactly those two, S-DOCTOR with standing 'PROPOSED to DR-111. Not admitted by this artifact.' and S-SARIF with 'PROPOSED. Preview advertises no SARIF. Not admitted here.' doesNot carries 'Does not self-admit doctor or SARIF as matrix rows.' Neither is moved into the admitted surface list.

attacksRun.attack: D-103 did not record what the subject says it recorded
attacksRun.evidence: Read live rather than inferred. The D-103 heading is 'Record compatibility-matrices-contract.v5 as DR-111's accepted design-contract candidate', its Subject pin is d0386cee, its Verdicts section carries both review paths and digests with ACCEPT 0 blockers 0 SHOULD-FIX, and its Decision states 'DR-111 stays OPEN. No SATISFIED. Numeric windows remain RESERVED. S-EVIDENCE remains deferred with DR-113. No lock is producible. D-056 Class A is not opened.' Every one of those clauses is reflected in the join without embellishment.

Checked field by field against live v5. sixCells is a six-element list, so 'six cells' is exact. noSharedVersion states there is no shared N/N-1/N-2 promise and no common version number. bridgesMean states a bridge MUST NOT wrap, translate, normalize, reorder, reinterpret, merge or assign new fates to semantic frames, which is the bridges-are-not-frame-translation rule the subject names. v5's authorityClaim itself describes 'the closed surface list for this closure', supporting the subject's 'closed surface list'.

Five obligations, each bucketed exactly once across summary's four lists - leftoverDesign, recordedCandidateNotApplied, specifiedNotLeftover and deferredOrRidesElsewhere - with no duplicates and none omitted. The two obligations with leftoverDesign true are exactly the two carrying rideStanding not-capable-of-riding, and the three with leftoverDesign false carry distinct non-riding standings appropriate to their kind. All five summary flags are the values the obligation bodies imply.

observationsNotFindings: The join's honesty is easiest to see where it would have been cheapest to overclaim. OBL-S-EVIDENCE and OBL-EXTRA-ROWS both carry leftoverDesign false, which could read as closure, but each pairs that with a rideStanding that says why - deferred-to-DR-113 and specified-not-leftover - so neither is presented as finished work on DR-111. The same discipline appears in OBL-CONTRACT-V5, where recording a candidate is explicitly separated from applying it.

OBL-LOCK-JOIN is the place a leftover join could most easily launder a proposal into law. Live v5's lockJoin carries an ATTRIBUTION paragraph recording that only the narrower rule is D-013-accepted and that the widening to exact-pin and cardinality is proposed, including in unaccepted schema successors. The subject preserves that by opening 'v5 lockJoin PROPOSES'. It does not reproduce the attribution detail, which it does not need to, but a coordinator reading only this join would not learn that the wider rule is unaccepted. Worth knowing when the DR-103 successor eventually consumes these windows.

T2-02 does not appear in file 08 at all; the classification lives in the pinned D-056 turn-2 draft. Anyone auditing the leftoverDesignOpenStanding sentence against the register alone will not find the anchor, which is why I record here that it is real and sits at the draft's DR-101/107/111/112/117/120/121/122/124/125/126/127 row.

Live v5 carries eight surfaces while the join names five obligations. The gap is principled rather than an omission - the RESERVED and scoped surface closures are specified content of the contract with dispositions already fixed by D-002 and the live DR-124 row - but the arithmetic looks like a shortfall until that is checked, so I record the reasoning rather than leave it implicit.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. The artifact presents two claims that could carry it, and both hold. Its quotation of v5's numericWindows is byte-equal to live v5 under == comparison, and the second inline rendering quotes only the text after 'RESERVED. ' while asserting that status outside the quotation, which is an honest split rather than a truncation - an initial mismatch I saw was my own regex breaking on the apostrophe in D-012's, not a defect. Its 'dual ACCEPT 0/0' standing checks out against both v5 verdict files, whose three advisories I read and which concern honestyRepairsFrom* naming rather than blockers. All 7 recordedInputs and 5 structured pins recompute with zero mismatches. Because a leftover join is a completeness claim I tested it as one: live v5 has eight surfaces against the join's five obligations, but the RESERVED and scoped closures - S-ROLE, S-RUST2, S-STATE - have dispositions already fixed by D-002 and the live DR-124 row and are specified contract content, unlike numericWindows which v5 explicitly declines to mint and leaves ownerless. Independently, the five obligations map one-to-one onto what D-103 actually recorded: DR-111 stays OPEN, no SATISFIED, windows RESERVED, S-EVIDENCE deferred with DR-113, no lock producible. The T2-02 reference in leftoverDesignOpenStanding looked unanchored because T2-02 occurs zero times in file 08, but it is anchored in the pinned D-056 turn-2 draft, which classifies DR-111 under 'No accepted T2-02 contract' - so calling the authoring limb stale while the windows limb remains is exactly right. No window value appears anywhere, QUALIFIED occurs zero times, all six SATISFIED occurrences are denials or eligibility framing, and both DR-G occurrences are denials. 17 attacks run, 17 refuted.
